concept.title: Your own fonts, colours and logo

conbody.p: stylesheetyour ownfontschangingcolourslogoargs.cssThe branding modes in are complete identities. Most publishers want something smaller: the neutral output with their own typeface, their own colours and their own logo in the masthead. That needs no change to the plugin, only a stylesheet of a few rules added to the build command.

section.title: Adding a stylesheet to the build
section.p: The govuk transformation takes the toolkit's standard stylesheet parameters. Name the stylesheet, say which folder it is in, and ask for it to be copied into the output:
On Windows the same command, on one line, with a Windows folder:

strow.stentry: The stylesheet's file name. One stylesheet; join several into one file.
The folder that holds it, as a full path. A relative path is not read from the folder you run the command in.
yes copies the stylesheet into the output. Without it the pages link to a file that is not there.
Optional: a folder inside the output to copy it to, such as theme. Left out, the stylesheet sits at the top of the output, beside index.html.

section.p: Every page then links the stylesheet after the Design System's stylesheet, the plugin's own, and the overlay of whichever branding mode is in use. That covers topic pages, the home page, the search, glossary and index pages, the figure and table lists, and the print document. A rule in your stylesheet therefore beats a rule of equal weight in any of those, with no need for !important. The one stylesheet that follows yours is the search component's own, on the search page only; style the search results through the component's custom properties, as the sample does, not by restyling its parts.
section.note: If the toolkit cannot find the stylesheet it says nothing and the pages are built without it. When your styles do not appear, look in a page's source for the link to your file: if there is none, the path in args.cssroot or the name in args.css is wrong.

section.title: What to override
section.p: Two stylesheets set the look. The Design System's reads most of its colours from CSS custom properties, which you set once on :root. The plugin's own furniture — the masthead, the sidebar, the contents lists, and links in topic text that the toolkit generates — carries classes that begin app- and sets its colours directly, so those need a rule each.

strow.stentry: font-family on .govuk-template [class*="govuk-"]. The Design System sets its font on each of its classes, so a rule on body alone changes little. The search results take theirs from --pagefind-ui-font on .app-search .pagefind-ui.
background on .app-masthead, and color on .app-masthead__title for the publication's name.
--govuk-brand-colour: the rule above the footer, and the Design System components that use the brand colour.

--govuk-link-colour, --govuk-link-hover-colour and --govuk-link-visited-colour for Design System links; and color on .app-sidebar__nav a, .app-contents a, .ullinks a, .linklist a, .related-links a and #main-content a:not([class]), with their :hover states, for the plugin's.
A ::before on .app-masthead__title with the logo as its background image. The masthead's one link keeps the publication's name as its text, so the logo needs no text of its own.

section.p: Code keeps its monospace font (pre.codeblock, code, samp and kbd set their own), and text inside a diagram keeps the font the drawing names.

section.title: A sample stylesheet
section.p: This stylesheet changes all three: a typeface from fonts the reader already has, a green brand colour for the masthead, links and footer, and a logo in front of the publication's name. Copy it and change the values in its first section. It is docs/manual/samples/custom.css in , where every change to the plugin is built with it and checked for accessibility.

dlentry.dd: The plugin's accessibility checks cover its own styles, not yours. Keep a contrast of at least 4.5 to 1 between text and its background, on the masthead as well as the page, and leave the yellow focus state alone. Check the result before you publish; describes what remains the publisher's responsibility.

The toolkit copies the stylesheet and nothing else. A logo or font file named in a url() is looked for relative to the stylesheet in the output, so copy those files there after the build. A logo written into the stylesheet as a data: URL, as in the sample, needs no second file.

dlentry.dt: Fonts and logos you may use
dlentry.dd: Host only a font whose licence allows web publication, and do not use a stylesheet to bring in the GOV.UK crown, GDS Transport or the NHS identity unless your organisation is entitled to them ().
With govuk.csp=meta the pages load stylesheets, fonts and images from the site itself, and images from data: URLs. A font fetched from another website is blocked; host the files with the site ().
Your stylesheet applies when a page is printed and in the print document too, so the typeface carries over to paper. The masthead, and the logo with it, is not printed.

The sample is written for the default neutral mode. The iStandUK, NHS and official modes already place a logo in the masthead and set their own colours; your stylesheet is still linked last in those modes, but leave out the sample's logo and masthead rules there.
